line: You folded all night waiting for a real hand. When kings finally came, you raised, and everyone folded.
He folds for an hour, then raises, and the whole table folds. They didn't read his cards. They read his clock.
Card dead for hours, finally ace-king, all in, and ace-queen hits a queen. That wasn't the hand that knocked you out.
If you've ever got so bored folding that you played seven-four just to feel something, the problem started long before the seven-four.
Ten minutes into the session: aces, all in, he calls with jack-ten off and rivers a straight. Was that a bad beat, or a normal Tuesday?
Your friend who swears his aces always get cracked? He's not cursed. He's just counting.
You got pocket aces all in before the flop, and lost to five-two offsuit. That wasn't the app being rigged. It was supposed to happen.
Everyone remembers the night their aces got cracked. Nobody remembers all the nights they held.
Top set, all in on the turn, against one flush draw. The whole table stands up for the river. That flush comes in 20% of the time.
You fold your flush draw to a big bet and the heart comes on the river. Most players call that fold a mistake. Most of the time it's the right one.
